summary: # 【Marvelous Designer】Learning Day - Hat Making Collection p03 Pure Enjoyment Edition 2_Sun Hat ## Introduction In this session, we will explore how to modify a dress hat into a women's woolen hat using Marvelous Designer. ## Modifying the Hat ### Disassembly and Simulation First, we need to delete the excess fake stitches. After that, we will simulate the modifications by pressing the control key. Once we finish with the disassembly and simulation, let's freeze the hat. ### Adjusting the Top Plate We will modify the top plate first. To create a round hat top, select the round plate. Activate the center point and drag the frame to form a smaller circle. ### Length Calculation and Adjustment After forming a smaller circle, we need to adjust the side. First, we must calculate its length, which can be seen in the attribute editor. Use the change length tool to modify the length of this side to match the length of the small plate. ### Curve Adjustment After the modification, it should resemble the magician hat. We need to adjust the curve so that the corresponding position of the side seam forms a state close to a right angle. Once completed, we will start the simulation. ### Editing Curve Points After the simulation, we need to use the tool to edit the curve points. Continue adjusting the curves of the bottom and top sides to achieve a right angle effect. ## Height Modification ### Shortening the Height Next, we want to shorten the height. Select the peak on the top and cut it. After cutting, we can delete the excess part and re-create the sewing line. ### Adjusting the Sewing Line After sewing, since we recreated the sewing line, the folding angle of the sewing line returns to 180 degrees, resulting in a round top. ### Side Width Adjustment Next, we will adjust the width of the side of this board to be more narrow. To match the length of the round top, we need to modify its length. Additionally, we can press the Ctrl key to slide along the side of the diagonal to form a right angle. ## Simulation and Design Refinement ### Adjusting the Curve Because the curve will affect our adjustment, we can delete the excess curve first and only keep some of the middle parts. After finishing the simulation, if there are any issues with the design, we need to modify it accordingly. ### Angle Adjustment First, we will continue to adjust the angle along the side to ensure the other side is correct. Once the top two corners are close to 90 degrees, we can turn it over and increase or decrease the angle as needed. ### Reference Curve Use this curve as a reference to adjust the curve of the bottom. If any part of the area is wider than desired, we can continue to adjust the curve. If the width on the side seems too short, we can lengthen the straight line in the back middle. ## Final Adjustments ### Simulating Smoke and Fire Next, we simulate the smoke and fire effects so that they can be simulated together. ### Adding Accessories We can now add the butterfly knot from our library window. In the Hardware and Trims section, we can find the Ribbon file. If it’s empty, we can click the download button in the upper right corner. ### Downloading Files We can download the whole thing or specific objects separately. If the selection box is gray, we can click the small arrow to download it. ### Placing the Butterfly Knot Double click the butterfly knot file and add it to the work area. Select the original position for placement. After adding it, select the water glue tool in the upper right corner and click on the hat plate to attach the butterfly knot on top of the hat. ### Deformation Tool Click the deformation tool in the upper right corner and drag the axis on the positioning ball to adjust the position of the butterfly knot. ## Creating the Bag Effect ### Drawing Lines If we want to create a bag effect, select the bottom side of this section and right-click to draw a line along the inner line. Then, cut this line off. ### Adjusting Texture Drag this line along the inner line of the butterfly knot. If it’s just the texture surface, our board will not appear thick, only showing the front and back. After cutting, switch to the thick texture surface to display the board’s thickness in the 3D window. ### Increasing Board Thickness We will increase the thickness of the board so it appears like there is a layer of tape outside. We can also enable the double layer display for a two-layer structure. ### Foldable Angle Adjustment Use the foldable angle tool to find the foldable angle, which is a spatial angle. This helps to identify the tape and the hat body easily. We can copy a fabric and apply it to the tape. ## Finalizing the Design ### Adjusting the Folding Angle Finally, we will re-set the angle of folding between the fern string to give the hat a downward angle that covers the design. Based on our fold angle calculation, we want to reduce the folding angle from 270 to 240 degrees. ### Butterfly Knot Position Lastly, adjust the position of the butterfly knot. Select it and set its intensity to 0 on the 3D fountain line on the right to eliminate the fountain line effect at the joint. Regarding thickness, the higher this value, the more pronounced the effect of the fountain line will be. Set it to 0 for a clean finish.
